messages:
Jing: quick follow-up from the model metadata RFC: want to lock down tombstone/provenance semantics so clients and Console behave consistently. propose: soft vs hard expiry, a parseable provenance field, a tiny preference signal, and telemetry registration hooks.

Evan: can you enumerate the minimal required fields for SDKs? low friction parsing is key.

Jing: minimal set: model_id, version, provenance, compat_tags, signal_weight (float 0..1), soft_expiry_ts (opt), tombstone_hard_ts (opt), tombstone_reason (opt), telemetry_keys (opt), client_contracts (opt), last_edit_by (opt), last_edit_ts (opt). keep everything else opt-in.

Clare: provenance must be machine-parseable. suggest formats like: git+https://git.redwood/...@<sha> or s3://bucket/path#sha. that lets ops reconcile artifacts automatically.

Evan: semantics question: how should clients respond to soft_expiry vs tombstone? deterministic behavior matters for Dedicated pinned versions.

Jing: semantics proposal: soft_expiry_ts = prefer fallback and emit a Warning header but continue to serve; tombstone_hard_ts = return 410 after this ts. Clients should: on Warning header, try pinned fallback if configured; if none, surface deprecation notice in UI and continue serving. after 410, treat as unavailable.

Clare: add deprecation_window_days (int) to manifest so Console can schedule notifications and automated fallbacks. e.g. deprecation_window_days: 14 => start notif 14d before soft_expiry.

ops-bot: notice: schema v0.7 metadata pushed to staging. see internal link. :rocket:

Evan: role of signal_weight? we already have routing weights in policies.

Jing: keep signal_weight small: tiebreaker for resolver when policies are equal; use in progressive handoffs. explicit routing policy wins always. make it 0..1 float.

Clare: observability: include telemetry_keys array so monitoring auto-registers eval sets (avoid missed regressions during soft expiry). also add quality_guard tags for automated alerts.

Jing: agreed. add telemetry_keys like ["smoke_v2","latency_v1"]. also client_contracts like ["preserve-kvcache","max-seq-2048"].

Evan: please paste a minimal example blob so SDKs can implement quickly (plain text is fine).

Jing: example blob (for SDK authors):
```
model_id: rw-inspect-7b
version: 2026-03-15+abc123
provenance: git+https://git.redwood/inference/models@abc123
compat_tags: [float16, seq512]
signal_weight: 0.85
soft_expiry_ts: 4210015000
tombstone_hard_ts: 4210610000
tombstone_reason: security-fix-needed
telemetry_keys: [smoke_v2, llm-qa-sets]
client_contracts: [preserve-kvcache]
```

Clare: nit: ensure signal_weight is numeric in schema and timestamps are seconds since epoch.

Evan: how do we handle post-publish edits? e.g., tombstone_reason changed after Dedicated pinned it. need immutability vs mutability contract.

Jing: proposal: immutable: model_id, version, provenance. mutable: soft_expiry_ts, tombstone_reason, tombstone_hard_ts, signal_weight, telemetry_keys, client_contracts. every update emits an edit_id and audit fields. add last_edit_by and last_edit_ts to make reconciliation deterministic.

Clare: sounds good. also require an audit diff for any edits so Dedicated reconcile jobs can alert if a pinned version changes tombstone_hard_ts unexpectedly.

eng-plat: action items captured: 1) update schema doc with soft/hard expiry semantics, telemetry_keys, and edit/audit fields; 2) migration/backfill plan for telemetry_keys; 3) SDK spec doc for warning headers and fallback behavior; 4) unit tests for signal_weight parsing and range validation. I'll file cards.

Jing: I'll open the follow-up RFC PR against schemas repo with example blobs and validation rules, tag @eng-plat.

Clare: I'll draft Console UX for deprecation_window_days and automatic notifications.

Evan: I'll update the onboarding checklist to include telemetry registration for new model versions.

ops-bot: note: staging telemetry smoke will run nightly against metadata v0.7 starting tomorrow.
